answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The atlas holds work receipts rather than names, so the tide of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, re-queued for a second panel, rewards vest against future work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the relic of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
